title: Bloom-to-Pattern Matrix
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Bloom's Taxonomy
Interaction Patterns
Instructional Design Checkpoint
MicroSim Design
description: A custom HTML table generated from a JSON array: six Bloom levels by appropriate patterns, inappropriate patterns and example MicroSims from the book, with clickable chips that open an explanation, a sketch and a reason, row tooltips with verb lists, and a Mismatch detective mode with a running score.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers and learning-technology developers

educational.topic: Matching interaction patterns to Bloom levels
learningObjectives: Differentiate appropriate from inappropriate interaction patterns for each Bloom level.
Explain why a mismatched pattern fails its objective.

technical.framework: HTML, CSS and JavaScript (no external library)

accessibility.notes: Chips are HTML buttons (keyboard focusable); the detail panel is aria-live.

controls.label: Row tooltip with the level's verbs

simulation.modelType: Clickable comparison matrix with quiz mode

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore a comparison matrix, then diagnose mismatches
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Comparison matrix with detail panel and diagnostic quiz
keyQuestions: Which patterns let the learner produce the performance the level asks for?
What evidence would a mismatched pattern fail to produce?
commonMisconceptions: A richer simulation is always better, whatever the objective.
Any activity with a score is a good Evaluate activity, even without feedback on reasons.
assessmentOpportunities: Written diagnosis of a new mismatched MicroSim description.
